scenes.headline: Your password can be phished. A passkey is built not to be.
scenes.body: New data from 15 big services, explained simply
scenes.say: Still typing passwords? This one is for you. New data from fifteen big online services shows passkeys are taking over. Here is what a passkey is, and why it matters.

scenes.headline: FIDO Alliance publishes its 2026 Passkey Index
scenes.body: 15 services took part, including Amazon, Google, Microsoft, PayPal, TikTok and WhatsApp
scenes.say: On October fifteenth, the FIDO Alliance, the industry group behind passkeys, published its twenty twenty-six Passkey Index. Fifteen services took part, including Amazon, Google, Microsoft, PayPal, TikTok and WhatsApp.

scenes.headline: of successful sign-ins now use a passkey
scenes.body: Up from 26% in 2025. FIDO calls the comparison directional: the group of services changed.
scenes.say: Thirty-six percent of successful sign-ins at these services now use a passkey, up from twenty-six percent last year. FIDO calls that comparison directional, because the group of services changed.

scenes.headline: A secret key stored on your device
scenes.body: You unlock it with the fingerprint, face or PIN you already use. It can sync across your devices.
scenes.say: So what is a passkey? It is a secret key stored on your device. You unlock it with the same fingerprint, face or PIN you already use, and it can sync across your devices.

scenes.headline: How a sign-in works
items: The site asks your device to prove it's you
You unlock with face, fingerprint or PIN
Your device proves it holds the key
No password typed, no shared secret
scenes.say: Here is a sign-in. The site asks your device to prove it is you. You unlock with your face, fingerprint or PIN. Your device proves it holds the key. No password is typed, and there is no shared secret on the server to steal.

scenes.headline: Codes can be relayed. Passkeys are designed not to be.
scenes.body: UK NCSC: all traditional MFA methods are “inherently phishable”
scenes.say: Why does this beat phishing? Britain's National Cyber Security Centre, the NCSC, says all traditional multi-factor methods are inherently phishable. Passkeys remove the ability to cheaply reuse or relay a login.

scenes.headline: of passkey sign-ins succeed
scenes.body: vs 78% for passwords and traditional MFA
scenes.say: They also just work. Ninety-three percent of passkey sign-ins succeed, against seventy-eight percent for passwords and traditional multi-factor codes.

scenes.headline: saved per sign-in, on average
scenes.body: Nearly three times faster than signing in without a passkey
scenes.say: And they are quicker. On average, a passkey sign-in saved twenty-seven seconds, nearly three times faster.

scenes.headline: All 8 services that measure phishing saw fewer successful attacks
scenes.body: After deploying passkeys. FIDO gives no percentage.
scenes.say: Most important: all eight services that measure phishing reported fewer successful attacks after deploying passkeys.

scenes.headline: “Consumers' first choice of login across all digital services”
scenes.say: In April, the NCSC said passkeys should now be consumers' first choice of login across all digital services.

scenes.headline: A passkey only helps if you actually use it.
scenes.body: At 8 of 10 services reporting both, passkey use still lags enrolment. If the old password stays the easy way in, that is what phishers will ask for.
scenes.say: Analyst note: a passkey only helps if you actually use it. At eight of the ten services that reported both numbers, passkey use still lags behind enrolment. If the old password stays the easy way in, that is what phishers will ask for.

scenes.headline: Do this tonight
items: Add a passkey to your main email account
Pick the passkey when you sign in
No passkey offered? Turn on two-step verification
scenes.say: Do this tonight. Add a passkey to your main email account first, because it can reset everything else. Then your shopping and payment accounts. When you sign in, pick the passkey. And where a site offers no passkey yet, turn on two-step verification.
